title: System Design Interview
blurb: System design from zero to interview-ready: the building blocks, estimation, a four-step framework, every classic design from rate limiter to file sync, more modern designs, and 60 practice prompts.
sources: Alex Xu, System Design Interview: An Insider's Guide (2nd ed.), ch. 1-16 (topic guide; all wording original)
DeCandia et al., Dynamo: Amazon's Highly Available Key-value Store (SOSP 2007)
Stripe engineering blog: rate limiters and idempotency (stripe.com/blog)

modules.title: 1. System design from zero
modules.summary: Clients, servers and requests; the database, cache, load balancer, queue and CDN; scaling, latency, throughput, availability and consistency in plain words.

lessons.title: Clients, servers and requests: what a "system" is
The five building blocks: database, cache, load balancer, queue and CDN
The vocabulary of scale: scaling, latency, throughput, availability and consistency

modules.title: 2. Scaling from zero to millions of users
modules.summary: From one machine to a replicated, cached, multi-data-centre, sharded architecture, one justified step at a time.

lessons.title: Scaling from zero I: from one server to a replicated, cached system
Scaling from zero II: stateless servers, data centres, queues, observability and sharding

modules.title: 3. Back-of-the-envelope estimation
modules.summary: Powers of two, latency and availability numbers, and QPS, storage, bandwidth and server-count estimates worked step by step.

lessons.title: Estimation I: the numbers worth memorising
Estimation II: QPS, storage and bandwidth worked step by step

modules.title: 4. A framework for the system design interview
modules.summary: The four steps (scope, high-level design, deep dive, wrap-up), the time budget, dos and don'ts and a complete worked session.

lessons.title: A framework for the interview I: the four steps
A framework for the interview II: dos, don'ts and a complete worked session

modules.title: 5. Design a rate limiter
modules.summary: Token bucket, leaky bucket, fixed window, sliding window log and sliding window counter; then the distributed design with shared counters, atomicity and failure policy.

lessons.title: Design a rate limiter I: requirements and the five algorithms
Design a rate limiter II: the distributed design

modules.title: 6. Design consistent hashing
modules.summary: The rehashing problem, the hash ring, virtual nodes, replication on the ring, and the alternatives: rendezvous hashing, jump hash and slot directories.

lessons.title: Design consistent hashing I: the rehashing problem and the ring
Design consistent hashing II: virtual nodes, replication and alternatives

modules.title: 7. Design a key-value store
modules.summary: CAP, partitioning, replication, tunable quorums, vector clocks, gossip, hinted handoff, Merkle trees and the LSM storage engine.

lessons.title: Design a key-value store I: CAP, partitioning, replication and quorums
Design a key-value store II: versioning, failure handling and the storage engine

modules.title: 8. Design a unique ID generator
modules.summary: Multi-master auto-increment, UUIDs, ticket servers and Snowflake-style IDs: bit layout, clocks, sequence overflow and machine-ID assignment.

lessons.title: Design a unique ID generator I: requirements and the four approaches
Design a unique ID generator II: the Snowflake design in depth

modules.title: 9. Design a URL shortener
modules.summary: Estimates, 301 vs 302, the data model, base-62 encoding, hashing with collision resolution, caching and abuse handling.

lessons.title: Design a URL shortener I: requirements, API, data model and base 62
Design a URL shortener II: code generation, collisions, caching and failure handling

modules.title: 10. Design a web crawler
modules.summary: The crawl loop, the URL frontier with politeness and priority, robots.txt, duplicate detection with Bloom filters, freshness and spider traps.

lessons.title: Design a web crawler I: requirements, the crawl loop and the high-level design
Design a web crawler II: the URL frontier, deduplication, freshness and robustness

modules.title: 11. Design a notification system
modules.summary: Push, SMS and email channels, third-party providers, queues per channel, deduplication, retries, rate limits, templates and user preferences.

lessons.title: Design a notification system I: channels, requirements and the high-level design
Design a notification system II: reliability, deduplication, retries and limits

modules.title: 12. Design a news feed system
modules.summary: Feed publishing and retrieval, fan-out on write vs fan-out on read, the hybrid for celebrity accounts, the cache layers and ranking.

lessons.title: Design a news feed I: requirements, API, data model and the two flows
Design a news feed II: fan-out strategies, caching and failure handling

modules.title: 13. Design a chat system
modules.summary: Polling, long polling and WebSocket; stateful connection servers, message storage, ordering with per-channel sequence numbers, multi-device sync and presence.

lessons.title: Design a chat system I: connections, requirements and the high-level design
Design a chat system II: message flow, ordering, sync and presence

modules.title: 14. Design a search autocomplete system
modules.summary: Tries with cached top-k, the data-gathering pipeline, the query service, sharding the trie, freshness and filtering.

lessons.title: Design search autocomplete I: requirements and the trie
Design search autocomplete II: building, serving, sharding and updating

modules.title: 15. Design a video platform
modules.summary: Upload, transcoding as a DAG, the bitrate ladder and adaptive streaming, CDN delivery and cost control, resumable uploads and safety.

lessons.title: Design a video platform I: requirements, upload and streaming flows
Design a video platform II: transcoding, adaptive bitrate, CDN cost and failures

modules.title: 16. Design a file storage and sync service
modules.summary: Block-level storage, delta sync, deduplication, metadata consistency, notifications, conflicts and storage cost.

lessons.title: Design file storage and sync I: requirements, blocks and the high-level design
Design file storage and sync II: delta sync, consistency, conflicts and failures

modules.title: 17. Building blocks in depth
modules.summary: Load-balancing algorithms, caching strategies and invalidation, database choice and indexing, replication and partitioning, CAP and PACELC, queues vs streams, idempotency, API styles and observability.

lessons.title: Building blocks I: load balancing algorithms and caching strategies
Building blocks II: database choice, indexing, replication and partitioning
Building blocks III: CAP and PACELC, queues vs streams, and idempotency
Building blocks IV: API styles, resilience patterns and observability

modules.title: 18. More designs
modules.summary: Ride-hailing dispatch, a payment system with idempotency and ledgers, ticket booking with seat locking, metrics and monitoring, a distributed job scheduler, ML model serving and a RAG application.

lessons.title: Design ride-hailing dispatch
Design a payment system: idempotency and ledgers
Design a ticket-booking system: seat holds and overselling
Design a metrics and monitoring system, and a distributed job scheduler
Design an ML model-serving platform and a RAG/LLM application

modules.title: 19. System design interview essentials
